name: Box64 BOX32 mode: dynarec code buffer is hinted at 0x100000000 so it does NOT consume the guest's 32-bit address space
required_postconditions: the code buffer must be at or above 4 GiB, the exact complement of the guest requirement that everything be below 4 GiB
the preferred path walks Box64's own MEM_RESERVED ranges from a static cursor starting at 0x100000000 and MAP_FIXEDs into them
the buffer is RWX and is never flipped

failure_sink.description: the MAP_FIXED path logs 'Error allocating Dynarec memory: %s' and returns MAP_FAILED to the caller, which then reports 'Cannot create dynamic map' and disables dynarec for that block.

source_locations.symbol: static uintptr_t cur = 0x100000000LL; - the search cursor starts exactly at 4 GiB
InternalMmap(box64_isAddressSpace32?NULL:(void*)0x100000000ULL, size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC, map_flags, fd, offset) - fallback hint

extraction_limitations: the 2 MiB size comes from DYNMMAPSZ at the caller, not from box32_dynarec_mmap itself.

'must be >= 4 GiB' is not expressible in this schema. It is encoded here only as a non-binding hint address; the analyzer has no way to know a lower placement would be a correctness failure rather than a harmless relocation.

x_campaign.rationale: A hinted RWX mapping at 4 GiB is unremarkable on x86-64 Linux, and the code accepts relocation, so nothing here can fail.
x_campaign.note_after_schema_fix: The complement of the box32 bound, now expressible.
